newsitem.title: UK: Gasoline traders prepare for possible U.K. tax hike.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline traders prepare for possible U.K. tax hike.

text.p: Speculation that Britain's post-election budget may include a tax increase on gasoline is encouraging oil companies and trading houses to build stocks of duty-paid fuel, oil traders said on Wednesday.
The new Labour government said it would present a mini-budget within two months of the election of May 1, but has declined to confirm that it will be on June 10, widely seen as the most likely date.
"There is an expectation that there will be a (gasoline) duty increase but no-one really knows," said a trader for a major oil company.
"But there is a lot of talk about it and you can see its effects in the market already."
On Wednesday, the premium for Northwest European gasoline delivered in June widened to around $5.00 over July, indicating that traders are starting to hoard June barrels.
"A lot of people are looking at (a budget increase) and that's why the June/July spread is firming up," a trader said.
Despite fierce competition at Britain's petrol pumps, duty increases are invariably passed directly on the consumer.
Some traders are expecting a tax hike of around two to three pence a litre.

At this level, retailers could look forward to pocketing an additional $35 to $50 a tonne on gasoline taxed at pre-budget levels sold after the budget -- equivalent to around one-fifth of current Rotterdam spot prices.
